summary: Orchestrated demotion plan for sustained concurrency surge after optimizer profile change
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a repeated increase in 95th/99th percentile latency and request timeouts for long-lived conversational sessions after enabling a new optimizer profile (aggressive async batching + KV prefetch + mixed-precision quant profile). Impact: Several users experiencing degraded UX, spawning retries and increased cost. Scope: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, traffic spike correlated with nightly batch job and many concurrent streaming sessions.

Environment: TempoHealth dedicated cluster (prod) serving redwood-open-13b-quant-ptq-v1 pinned on route /v1/generate.

Observed behavior: After optimizer profile rollout at 2026-03-11T23:40Z, autoscaler performed several scale-ups but latency remained elevated for long sessions. We see partial failures (502/504) and occasional 5xx during KV eviction windows. Customer requests a safe, orchestrated rollback/demotion plan that minimizes dropped sessions and avoids large reheats or cache stampedes.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Route traffic to TempoHealth dedicated pool with optimizer profile 'aggressive-mixed-async-ptq-v2' enabled on /v1/generate.
2) Run concurrent streaming workloads: 300 active long-lived chat sessions with average token rate 6/sec and periodic prefix changes.
3) Observe 95p/99p latency and retry rate spike after 15-30 minutes; note intervals of KV eviction and increased GPU memory pressure.
4) Correlate with autoscaler events and optimizer telemetry (batch sizes growing beyond safe limits).
logs: Relevant traces attached: request_ids: r-20260312-0001, r-20260312-0048. Sample error: 'kvcache: eviction during active prefix write -> downstream buffer overflow' and 'serving-runtime: async batch overflow -> 504 gateway timeout'. Full debug logs uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/tempohealth/SUP-990777/logs/2026-03-12.tar.gz
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 02:15 - Support: Initial triage shows latency increase begins ~15 minutes after profile flip. No infra maintenance at time of event.

2026-03-12 03:00 - SRE hypothesis: Aggressive async batching allowed batch sizes to grow with long-lived sessions, increasing per-batch compute and triggering KV prefetch evictions under memory pressure.

2026-03-12 04:10 - Findings: Memory pressure correlated with KV cache TTL expiry during high concurrency; eviction spikes align with the onset of 5xx errors. Quant profile appears compatible but amplifies memory usage slightly due to larger internal buffer allocations.
2026-03-13 09:20 - Networking check: No significant packet loss; connection stability within expected bounds.

2026-03-13 11:40 - Safety note: Direct immediate disable of optimizer feature 'kv-prefetch' will cause many sessions to rehydrate KV state and may increase downstream load; recommend staged demotion with traffic gating and circuit fences.
comments: 2026-03-12 05:02 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thanks for the report. We're coordinating an SRE-led demotion plan that avoids a hard rollback. Can you confirm whether you have per-tenant snapshots enabled and whether traffic split is possible on your side?

2026-03-12 05:44 - TempoHealth (Customer): We can do a 10/90 traffic split for a single route and we have per-tenant snapshots enabled. We prefer minimal session disruptions; how long will staged demotion take?

2026-03-12 07:28 - Diego Morales (SRE): Proposed plan: 1) Gate new requests to a fallback model variant with conservative optimizer settings (async batching disabled, kv-prefetch off, quant profile: ptq-conservative). 2) Gradually re-route 10%->30%->60%->100% over 30-minute windows. 3) Run background warmup for KV cache for the fallback variant using shadow replays. 4) If incidents persist, snapshot rollback to pre-change optimizer profile. We'll orchestrate via console and provide toggle scripts.
2026-03-13 08:15 - Aisha Patel (Support): Implemented first 10% gate at 2026-03-13T08:00Z. Early metrics show 20% reduction in 95p latency on the gated cohort. Continuing to 30% at 08:40Z per plan.
2026-03-14 09:50 - TempoHealth (Customer): 100% roll to fallback completed; observed stable latencies for 24 hours. Please confirm closure checklist and any follow-ups.
resolution: Workaround and rollback executed: Staged demotion to conservative optimizer variant (async batching off, kv-prefetch disabled, quant profile rolled back to ptq-conservative) completed 2026-03-13. We used traffic gating (10/30/60/100) with 30-minute windows and background KV warmup via shadow replays to avoid mass rehydrates. Post-roll metrics: 95p latency reduced to baseline, error rate normalized. Follow-ups: (1) Run offline load test to tune a safer mixed-mode optimizer (ticketed as INT-23480), (2) Add an autoscaler health-check that halts aggressive batching if per-GPU memory > 78%, (3) Create a preflight sim job for optimizer flips for dedicated tenants. Customer satisfied and asked for a short runbook; authored draft and linked to related_confluence_pages. Marking as resolved pending customer confirmation for closure.
postmortem_actions: Create INT ticket for autoscaler health-check: INT-23480
Add gating flag to optimizer config UI (console): enable 'staged_demote' toggle
Document KV warmup shadow-replay steps in runbook
